newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico shares end firm on late foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico shares end firm on late foreign buying.

text.p: Mexico stocks closed higher on Friday, boosted by a wave of last-minute buying by foreign investors.
"The market felt very firm, and foreigners stepped in at the bell, albeit selectively," a desk trader said.
The blue chip IPC share index ended up 32.70 points, or 0.83 percent, at 3,968.81. On the broad market, gainers outstripped decliners by 57 to 29, out of 114 stocks that changed hands.
Trading volume looked deceptively high at 100.1 million shares, dealers said, because one single cross-trade accounted for 30 percent of that total.
Dealers said the market was quiet because many floor traders had gone to a convention held in the Caribbean resort town of Cancun.
"Many left on Thursday, and those left behind wanted to close early," a floor trader said.

Dealers said a recovery on Wall Street also helped trigger buying on the market. The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 0.86 point at 7,331.04 after rebounding from an earlier sell-off trigged by a profit warning from Intel Corp.

Retail chain Cifra contributed to most of the market's gains, as its blue chip B shares rose 16 centavos (2 cents) to 13.56 pesos ($1.71) on speculation the company would sell some of its holdings to Wal-Mart Stores Inc.

Telmex stock was also stronger, adding 14 centavos (2 cents) to 17.58 pesos ($2.22). The telecommunication provider's American Depository Receipts ended up 1/4 at 44-3/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Shares of troubled conglomerate Grupo Sidek and its subsidiaries were among the day's prominent losers, as investors fretted about a long-awaited debt restructuring programme expected to be announced at a shareholders' meeting on Friday.
Sidek's stock had gained recently on speculation that such a plan was ready, but the suspense as the news was awaited during the session sparked selling.
"There was too much speculation over the assembly, that's why (Sidek and Situr) fell," a trader said.
Sidek announced after the close of trade that it had restructured some $233 million of its debt.
Sidek B shares shed 6 centavos (less than 1 cent) to end at 60 centavos (8 cents), while its tourist arm Situr declined 2 centavos (less than 1 cent) to 41 centavos (5 cents).
Sidek agreed to hand over its stake in steelmaker Simec and shipbuilder Sinam to Situr, analysts present at the assembly told Reuters.
Simec ended up 1 centavo (less than 1 cent) at 1.43 pesos (18 cents).
